newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia expects IMF money after May board meeting.
newsitem.headline: Russia expects IMF money after May board meeting.

text.p: Russia expects the board of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to meet by mid-May and release money delayed from Russia's $10 billion loan, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Friday.

Dubinin told a briefing Russia would receive 500 million special drawing rights (SDR) -- about $685 million -- for the first quarter of this year, less than the $325 million a month Russia was receiving last year when money was being paid out at a higher rate.
Dubinin said the IMF would in future monitor the Russian economy on a quarterly rather than monthly basis, with money paid out from the loan on a quarterly basis.
An IMF mission working on Russia's 1997 economic programme has just completed its work in Moscow. Dubinin said the talks were successful.

The mission to review the Russia's performance in the second quarter would come in July, with funds disbursed in August. "We expect the Board of Directors to take a decision in the first half of May, or at least by mid-May," Dubinin said.

"This depends on when our documents arrive and how long it takes to examine these documents and the mission's report, and after that we will apparently receive all the tranches for the first quarter in a volume of 500 million SDR, and after that similar tranches will be received on a quarterly basis," he said.
